chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The years (ages) of the cow you sell are the same, and its aged one, with regards to the sacrifice, is equal.

key_terms.الْبَقَرِ: The cow (specifically referring to the species in sacrificial context)
key_terms.مُسِنُّهَا: Its aged one / the old one

ai.seo_question: What are the age requirements for a cow to be valid for sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the specific numerical age of a cow is not a strict prerequisite for its validity as a sacrificial animal, provided it meets the general criteria of maturity and health. It highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the 'years' (سنين) of cattle, distinguishing between the technical definition of age for sale versus the physical condition required for the ritual slaughter (dhabh). This emphasizes that the essence of the sacrifice lies in the animal's fitness rather than rigid chronological constraints.
